title: Any interest in forming a slop publishing group?
author: Aineisa
selftext:
I joke about the slop.

Here’s the pitch. 

I have a corporation registered in Canada and have used it to publish a couple non-AI games to steam which did alright.

With how powerful Claude and other AI generators are I think there is going to be a flood of AI games. Maybe it would be good to use the corp as a \*\*curator\*\* and publisher of good, interesting, AI made games. Something like a seal of quality that gamers can trust. 

Having these games under onè publisher would also allow us to create bundles in different genres, land would help gamers sort through the inevitable slop. 

What’s in it for the devs?   
\- No steam fee, the corp would cover that.   
\- A generous profit split.   
\- Being part of a group that gamers learn to trust. - Not have to handle steam store setup.   
\- Not have to handle business taxes or tax treaties.   
\- be a part of bundles   
\- and more

If interested send me a DM and let’s get some sort of organization going. If there are enough I’ll share a discord where we can discuss as a group.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: No offense but basically all you're offering is to cover a steam publishing fee for a cut of all profits? That sounds insane to me.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
Where did I say “all profits?” 

“Generous profit split” definitely doesn’t mean “all” so I have no idea where you got that idea. 

I think a 90/10 split would be fine but there would have to be a bit more discussion on what advertising each dev would want to do.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body:
are you purposefully not understanding what I wrote or what? how can you see "a cut of all profits" and then say "I didn't say all profits"? 

you really think 100$ and like maybe a days worth of effort to setup a steam page really warrants 90/10 spilt you're out of your mind

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
Ok maybe my idea was wrong. 

I still believe some curation needs to happen as the number of games published will skyrocket. 

It’s already hard to cut through steams algorithm and it’ll only get harder. 

Building an audience is what the future will be like and getting everything under the same banner, doesn’t have to be a corp or publisher, would be a good idea.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: I know I came on hard, but I do agree with most of these issues and the "how will anyone stand out when there are so many more games out there" is a good issue worth discussing.

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: What’s the generous profit split? The only way this works without scamming the people spending hours trying to make not slop ai games, you would have to have a standard split not something that changes depending on the game or the dev.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body: Yes definitely. It would be discussed with each person who signs up. Something like 90/10 would be fine but if the dev wants paid advertising that would have to be revised.

comments.author: Vindelator
comments.body: If the publisher puts 100k into the marketing budget for the game upfront, it could be a good deal for some people.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body: 100k for marketing an AI dev game? You’re really overestimating how much the average steam indie game makes.

replies.author: Vindelator
replies.body: What number do you think is appropriate for a publisher to invest in the project they will profit from? That is how publishing works.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
How traditional publishing works yes. 

I guess I wasn’t clear in my post that I only wanted to try setup something more like a group of game devs and not a hierarchical publishing house.

replies.author: Vindelator
replies.body:
You were crystal clear that you want your cut, but to don't want to invest.

Seems like a worse deal than the traditional model for the devs.

comments.author: mindless_token
comments.body: Are you going to promote signed games?

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
Paid ads? No unless the dev really wants it. 

Other marketing? Yes. I think there’s a benefit to having our games under onè umbrella. It means we can build an audience in onè place. 

Right now everyone is off trying to build their own audience. 

If we have a group it makes reaching a large audience easier. We could have regular “new game of the month” or “best of 2026” bundles and more. 

Remember that AI makes it super easy to generate games. The only way to cut through the slop is by combining and curating

replies.author: mindless_token
replies.body: Then theres no point joining. Thats what publishers provide in exchange for a cut.

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
I’m not carrying bags of cash here. 

AI is going to redefine how the whole industry works.

With AI making it so easy to create games it’ll be more important than ever to build a market and audience. 

I’m offering a way for game devs to group under a banner that hopefully gamers will trust as a producer of non-slop games made with AI.

currently am an fullstack ai enginner focusing on agents and agentic enginnering but would love to get back into game development now I fully understand how most games are made

comments.author: Aware-Source6313
comments.body: Here's my pitch: in the era of ai there will be many curators of slop games, many of them doing so with superficial quality checks. We need to create the curators. I will use my company as a seal of approval for quality curators. You give us 10% of your orgs profits and we handle posting on social media, and bundle games across all the curation companies under our umbrella. You find the devs, we'll handle the backend stuff on steam and coordinating with other curators. When volume gets this big, we need multi level curation to deliver value, and my org will rest on our humble little slice at the top of the pyramid.
